subject: Hindu Religious Education

source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — Hindu Religious Education Grade 7 (First published 2022, Reviewed 2024)
source.notes: designs/Hindu-Religious-Education-Grade-7-Design-Formatted-April-2024.pdf, provided by the user in the repo's designs/ folder. Read with the Read tool with NO pages parameter (poppler is unavailable in this environment); full text extracted natively across all 41 pages in one call. Strand/sub-strand structure verified verbatim against the design's own 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS' table (page x) and the six per-strand tables (pages 1-23). NOTE: Grade 7's sub-strand list does NOT mirror Grade 8 or Grade 9 HRE — it has 6 strands / 8 sub-strands, with Religious Practices and Yog each carrying two sub-strands.

essenceNote: HRE at Junior Secondary builds a sense of identity, belonging and self-inquiry across the physical, mental, moral, social and spiritual faculties. It teaches learners to build positive relationships and solve challenges collectively with care, empathy and respect for people of different heritages and religions, promoting religious freedom, diversity, inclusion and social cohesion (verbatim essence statement, page viii). The subject's general outcomes name four faiths throughout: Sanatan/Vedic, Jain, Buddhist and Sikh.

subStrands.name: Enlightened Beings
contentPool: Guru Har Rai Ji and Dara Shikoh
Lord Krishna saving the honour of the Pandavas in the Jungle
Guru Har Krishan Ji and Chhajumal
specificLearningOutcomes: narrate the listed stories of the Enlightened Beings for better understanding
explore the interrelationships of the Enlightened Beings for spiritual growth
illustrate the events mentioned in the lives of the Enlightened Beings for ease of understanding
appreciate the values taught by the Enlightened Beings for holistic development
keyInquiryQuestions: How do the teachings of Enlightened Beings contribute to uplifting society today?
Why is it important to adopt values drawn from the lives of Enlightened Beings?
learningExperiences: discuss and present the interrelationships of Enlightened Beings
use print and digital resources/digital resources with assistive technology to research on the stories of the Enlightened Beings
research using digital media/library/magazines/resource person(s), the events that each Enlightened Being underwent
draw or paint or make tactile cut-outs of the illustrations of events mentioned in the lives of Enlightened Beings to assist learners with special needs in class
participate in community service activities that lead to inclusivity, promotion of animal welfare and acts of kindness
coreCompetencies: Citizenship: socio-cultural sensitivity and awareness when exploring the interrelationships of the Enlightened Beings
Learning to Learn: sharing learnt knowledge when discussing and presenting interrelationships

Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: open-mindedness and creativity while using various media to research the lives of the Enlightened Beings, and while participating in animal welfare and mentorship programs
Digital Literacy: using print and digital resources/assistive technology to depict the stories
values: Social justice — cooperation in community service leading to inclusivity, animal welfare and acts of kindness
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — community service learning activities
English — speaking skills when discussing and presenting the events each Enlightened Being underwent
subStrands.assessmentSignal: The rubric's three indicators are narrate stories, explore INTERRELATIONSHIPS (exceeding = 'using diagrams'), and illustrate the EVENTS. Interrelationship and event-sequence questions are therefore required, not optional — recall of names alone does not meet the rubric.

subStrands.name: Scriptural texts
specificLearningOutcomes: distinguish the four selected Scriptural texts that promote peace and harmony
apply values from the four selected Scriptures in daily life for sustainable living
create content to share relevant Scriptural messages that foster peace and harmony
appreciate approaches for restoring peace and harmony in society as stipulated in the Scriptures
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are Scriptures important in our lives?
How do Scriptures promote peace and harmony in society?
learningExperiences: discuss with peers their findings from the research regarding the values drawn from different Scriptures
interact with resource persons on values from Scriptures, create audio/video recordings, and present the same in class
conduct research using digital media/digital media with assistive technology library/magazines to identify Scriptures that promote peace in society through Scriptural texts
create and present skits that address various approaches on how humankind can be more peaceful and harmonious
read and discuss with the parents/guardians how Scriptures promote peace and harmony
assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching basic concepts from Scriptures in their class
coreCompetencies: Citizenship: active community life skills when researching Scriptures that promote peace
Learning to Learn: self-reflection when creating and presenting skits on how humankind can be more peaceful
Digital Literacy Skills: digital citizenship when conducting research using digital media
values: Peace — calmness and respect for others during discussion and interaction with parents/guardians
Respect — patience when interacting with resource persons on values from Scriptures
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts and Sports — creating and presenting skits from Scriptural teachings
English — speaking skills when discussing research findings in groups
Social Studies — socialising with people of different social, cultural and religious backgrounds when visiting places of worship
scopeNotes: include: all FOUR texts are required — the rubric explicitly grades 'distinguishes all the four selected Scriptural texts', with three = approaching expectations and fewer than three = below expectations. A skill covering only two or three of the four texts fails the design's own bar.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric indicator 2 is 'ability to CREATE CONTENT to share relevant Scriptural messages' — the sub-strand is not purely recall; questions should reach applying/sharing a scriptural value in a real situation.

subStrands.name: Fundamental Principles
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths
examine the Scriptural stories based on the four selected Principles of Dharma for social cohesion
practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment
appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to learn principles of Dharma?
How can the Principles of Dharma be practised in our daily lives?
learningExperiences: create a game on the fundamental principles of Dharma using locally available resources (For example, Monopoly, Snakes and Ladders, and Word Puzzles)
discuss with peers the importance of compassion to road crash survivors/victims following the Principles of Dharma in their lives
dramatize the Scriptural stories based on the fundamental principles of Dharma that enhance spiritual uplift
visit animal shelters, homes for the elderly and orphanages to practice fundamental principles
visit places of worship and interact with resource person(s) to gain insight into the application of Principles of Dharma
assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching the lessons drawn from the Scriptural stories
coreCompetencies: Learning to Learn: developing relationships when creating games on the fundamental Principles of Dharma
Self-efficacy: interacting with technology when researching the importance of the Principles of Dharma
Creativity and Imagination: originality in creating games and dramatizing Scriptural stories
Citizenship: social and civil skills when visiting places of worship, homes of the elderly, orphanages and animal shelters
values: Love — generosity and hospitality when visiting orphanages/homes for the elderly and animal shelters
Responsibility — diligence in researching and applying the Principles of Dharma
linkedLearningAreas: English — writing and finding translations of the terminologies used in explaining the Principles of Dharma
Creative Arts and Sports — performing skits and creating games on the Principles of Dharma
Social Studies — taking care of the environment and animals
scopeNotes: include: the design's own gloss is binding — 'Pranidaya (compassion)' and 'Purusharth (hard work)'. Purusharth is glossed by KICD as hard work/self-effort at this grade, NOT as the classical four aims of life (dharma/artha/kama/moksha); do not silently substitute the classical meaning.
include: road-crash survivors/victims are named explicitly as the compassion application context — this is a KICD-supplied real-world framing, not an invented one.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric grades 'describes ALL the four selected Principles' (three = approaching). It also grades 'examines the Scriptural stories based on the Principles of Dharma WITH CORRECT EVIDENCE' — evidence-linked, story-grounded questions are required, not bare definitions.

subStrands.name: Buddhist Practices
contentPool: Paying homage to the Buddha (Buddha Vandana)
Taking refuge in the triple gem (Tisarana)
Metta meditation and sharing of merits
specificLearningOutcomes: examine the Buddhist daily scheduled practices for generalisation
illustrate the observance of the scheduled religious practices in daily life
practice the Buddhist scheduled religious practices in daily life
appreciate the benefits of the Buddhist daily scheduled practices for harmonious living
keyInquiryQuestions: How do daily scheduled practices benefit society?
How do meditation practices impact one's life?
learningExperiences: mention Buddhist daily scheduled practices
conduct research on the Buddhist daily scheduled practices using digital devices/resource persons/library
tabulate and make a presentation of the findings on Buddhist daily scheduled practices
participate in discussions with peers on individual findings on the benefits of each practice
visit the Vihar (Buddhist temple) and record a video/take photographs (with permission) of the daily scheduled practices and present it in class
recite Mantras used during scheduled practices
assist learners with special needs as per their abilities the religious practices carried out in a place of worship
coreCompetencies: Citizenship: socio-cultural sensitivity in group discussions on the benefits of each practice
Self-efficacy and Critical thinking: self-awareness, planning skills and critical thinking when tabulating and presenting findings
Digital Literacy: researching the Buddhist daily scheduled practices using digital devices
values: Peace — calmness while observing scheduled practices in the Buddhist faith
Respect — patience and appreciation of diverse opinions in group activities
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — interacting with individuals and resource persons from the Buddhist faith
Creative Arts and Sports — reciting mantras
English — speaking and reciting Mantras used during scheduled practices
scopeNotes: include: all SEVEN listed practices are in scope — the seven-item list is the hard floor on the fact pool for this sub-strand.

note: 'Samantha' is the design's spelling of Samatha (tranquillity/calm-abiding) and 'Suittanipata' of Sutta Nipata — KICD transliterations are used in learner-facing text, with the standard spelling noted where helpful.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Core Competencies explicitly name Critical thinking → an Analyze/Evaluate-tier branch is mandatory for this sub-strand, not optional. Rubric also grades 'illustrates the OBSERVANCE ... in daily life', i.e. applying the practice, not naming it.

subStrands.name: Places of Worship
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the practices conducted during the festivals at the places of worship for a deeper understanding
illustrate the religious practices of the four faiths for community integration
acknowledge commonalities within the religious practices for self-reflection
keyInquiryQuestions: How do celebrations of festivals at places of worship help in inculcating moral values in our life?
Why is it important to celebrate religious festivals at places of worship?
learningExperiences: use digital devices/digital devices with assistive technology for learners with special needs/resource persons/library, to conduct research on religious practices
attend at least one of the listed festivals and discuss their findings with peers
prepare and present a creative piece of artwork on their understanding of the commonalities of the religious practices in the four faiths
interact with a resource person(s) on the commonalities of the religious practices in the four faiths
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: attending at least one of the listed festivals
Digital Literacy: preparing and presenting creative artwork on the commonalities of the religious practices in the four faiths
values: Integrity — discipline and avoiding breaches of confidentiality and security when attending a festival
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts and Sports — preparing and presenting a creative piece of artwork on the commonalities of the religious festivals
scopeNotes: include: one festival per faith — Durga Pooja (Sanatan/Vedic), Ayambil (Jain), Vesak (Buddhist), GurPurab (Sikh). The COMMONALITIES across the four are an explicit outcome (c) in their own right, not a bonus.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric: 'outlines the practices conducted during the festivals ... SYSTEMATICALLY' (exceeding) vs 'without the CORRECT ORDER' (approaching). Sequence is directly graded here — an ordering-kind branch is the rubric-aligned interaction for this sub-strand.

subStrands.name: Concepts of Yog
specificLearningOutcomes: explore the three selected concepts of Yog for personal development
distinguish the three selected Yog concepts for better understanding
illustrate circumstances under which Yog is applicable in daily life
acknowledge the role of Yog for spiritual growth
keyInquiryQuestions: How is Yog beneficial in developing life skills?
Why is Yog significant in spiritual nourishment?
learningExperiences: use digital devices/digital devices with assistive software for learners with special needs/resource person(s)/library to research on the three different concepts of Yog
discuss with peers and present the findings in class
recite concept of Yog with the help of their parents/guidance and teacher
categorise and tabulate or write the different concepts of Yog
make a presentation to illustrate the circumstances under which Yog is applicable
participate in charitable activities that foster the three concepts of Yog
coreCompetencies: Digital literacy: researching the three different concepts of Yog
values: Responsibility — hard work when participating in charitable activities that foster the three concepts of Yog
linkedLearningAreas: English — speaking and reciting the concept of Yog with the help of parents/guardians and teacher
scopeNotes: include: the design names exactly THREE concepts (bhakti, jnana, karma) for Grade 7. Do not import the eight limbs of Ashtanga Yog or Raja Yog — they are not in this grade's design.
note: 'categorise and tabulate ... the different concepts of Yog' is an explicit learning experience — a categorize-kind branch is directly curriculum-endorsed here.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric grades exploring AND distinguishing all three concepts; outcome (c) 'illustrate CIRCUMSTANCES under which Yog is applicable in daily life' requires Apply-tier situational questions, not definitions.

subStrands.name: Path of Devotion (Bhakti Yog)
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the elements of Bhakti Yog as per the four faiths for a deeper understanding
explore the key activities of Bhakti Yog among the four faiths for self-development
practice the elements of Bhakti Yog for spiritual growth
acknowledge the role of Bhakti Yog for spiritual development
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is devotion important in our lives?
How can we use the key elements of Bhakti Yog to strengthen devotion?
learningExperiences: name element of Bhakti Yog as per the four faiths
interact with resource person(s) from the four faiths (Sanatan/Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh) to understand the key elements of Bhakti Yog
design and present a poster/chart/tactile illustration of their findings from the resource person
use digital devices/print media to capture devotional activities for discussion and performance (recite/sing/sign/dance)
compose and recite their own unique devotional poem for self-reflection
participate in activities that focus on faith and trust towards each other while practising Bhakti Yog
assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching basic meditation in Yoga
coreCompetencies: Creativity and Imagination: designing and presenting a poster/chart/tactile illustration of findings from the resource person
values: Social justice — cooperation in activities focused on faith and trust towards each other while practising Bhakti Yog
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts and Sports — designing and presenting a poster/chart
English — composing and reciting their own devotional poem
scopeNotes: include: the personal/communal split is the design's own structure — four personal elements (mantras, mala, meditation, chanting/recitation) and three named communal terms (Satsang, Sangha, Sangat), each belonging to a different tradition.
include: 'as per the FOUR faiths' recurs in three of the four outcomes — every element should be shown across Sanatan/Vedic, Jain, Buddhist and Sikh practice, not in one tradition only.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric indicator: 'describes the elements of Bhakti Yog as per the four faiths WITH RELEVANT EXAMPLES' — per-faith worked examples are what 'exceeding' looks like.

subStrands.name: Religious Ceremonies
specificLearningOutcomes: examine the three selected religious ceremonies performed in the four faiths
interpret the significance of the three selected religious ceremonies for social cohesion
participate in the religious ceremonies for social cohesion
appreciate the practice of religious ceremonies for cultural preservation
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are the religious ceremonies significant in modern society?
How do religious ceremonies contribute to the purification of the mind, body and soul?
learningExperiences: mention religious ceremonies performed by four faiths
use different digital devices/digital devices with assistive software for learners with special needs/print media to explore the following religious ceremonies

watch/listen to audio-visual clips or visit places of worship accompanied by elders/parents/guardians to gather more information on religious ceremonies in the four faiths from a resource person (priest/community management)
make a video/participate in making an audio-visual clip on the religious ceremonies which can be shown in class
write an essay for peer review on the traditions of religious ceremonies
sing/sign/listen to the songs/hymns/verses related to religious ceremonies
coreCompetencies: Digital Literacy: making a video/audio-visual clip on the religious ceremonies
Learning to learn: gathering information on religious ceremonies in the four faiths from a resource person (priest/community management)
values: Respect — etiquette when singing/signing/listening to the songs/hymns/verses related to religious ceremonies
linkedLearningAreas: English — writing an essay for peer review on the traditions of religious ceremonies
Creative Arts and Sports — singing/signing songs/hymns/verses related to religious ceremonies
scopeNotes: note: the sub-strand bullet list carries FOUR named ceremonies (Jatkaram, Naamkaran, Sikh naming, dastar bandhan) while the outcomes and rubric both say 'the three selected religious ceremonies'. The discrepancy is in the source. Resolution taken: teach all four named bullets — covering four cannot fail a rubric that grades three, whereas dropping one risks omitting a named item.
include: outcome (b) 'INTERPRET THE SIGNIFICANCE ... for social cohesion' — meaning-of-the-rite questions are required alongside procedure questions.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric grades interpreting the SIGNIFICANCE of the ceremonies 'with examples' at exceeding level; procedure recall alone only reaches the lower bands.

checked: root design doc 'more about svg usage per cbc curriculum'
visualCoverageDecision.finding: Assests-svg/ holds only animal, fruit, food and planet icons (svgrepo cartoon set) — nothing religious. The SVG design doc's Junior School section prescribes maths instruments, lab apparatus, hand tools, PPE, maps, charts and 3D solids; its only mention of Religious Education is inside a 'Social Studies & Religious Education' row that lists map work, the 47 counties and weather instruments — none applicable to HRE content. VisualSpec in web/src/lib/types.ts likewise carries no religious primitive.
visualCoverageDecision.decision: No SVG/photo visual built for any HRE Grade 7 skill. Declined for absence of a suitable, respectful primitive rather than absence of effort — depicting deities, Gurus, Tirthankars or the Guru Granth Sahib in generated cartoon SVG would risk misrepresenting sacred figures, and neither source sanctions it. Recorded inline in each skill file. Revisit only if the user commissions a purpose-made, community-reviewed HRE asset set.
